title: Divine Guidance
english: God works through the hands of saints to bring about His glory, and it is through His Spirit that He accomplishes this.
If the Spirit of God glorifies the Son, it is impossible for someone speaking in the Spirit to speak ill of Him.
On the other hand, those who attribute creation to someone other than the One through whom all things came into being would be completely without the Holy Spirit.
They explicitly say 'Anathema Jesus'.
In contrast, those who confess Jesus as God and Lord will be rightly guided by the Spirit, who searches all things, even the depths of God, and conveys this knowledge to the saints.

The apostle Paul testifies to this, saying that there are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit, and different kinds of service, but the same Lord, and different kinds of workings, but the same God who works all things in all (1 Corinthians 12:4-6).

Just as earthly rulers reward their loyal servants with various honors, so the Holy Trinity distributes the gifts of heavenly goods to those who love it with a pure heart and mind, through the Spirit, as through Christ, from the Father.
All things are given from the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit, and each person is given the manifestation of the Spirit for their benefit.
God knows the suitable times for each of the things He does, and all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Him, as it is written (Colossians 2:3).
To one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit.
In my opinion, the word of wisdom is the one that flows easily from a very fluent tongue, and it is characterized by being prompt and effortless.
To another person, the Spirit gives the word of knowledge.
There are some people who may not be able to speak easily or with boldness, but they are very deep in understanding and have a profound grasp of the sacred words.
They may not be able to teach others easily, but they are able to initiate them into the mysteries and interpret the things that have been contemplated.
The word of wisdom and the word of knowledge are both distributed by the one Spirit to those who are worthy, from the Father through the Son.
For to some of the holy apostles, He commanded to proclaim the word of faith to those from the blood of Israel, and to others, He assigned the lands of the Gentiles.

And indeed in the acts of the holy apostles it will be found written that while they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, 'Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them' (Acts 13:2).

This marked the beginning of Paul's apostleship to the nations, a ministry that he would later glorify in his writings, saying 'As long as I am an apostle of the nations, I glorify my ministry' (Romans 11:13).
Therefore, the Son distributes the ministries, and the Holy Spirit effects the thing with authority; for the Spirit is of the Son.
Thus, those who attribute creation to someone other than the One through whom all things came into being would be completely without the Holy Spirit, for they are not rightly guided by the Spirit.
translator_notes: The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off at the beginning or end.
The translation aims to preserve the original word order and meaning, while still conveying the author's intended message in natural literary prose.
The translation of Λειτουργούντων as 'ministering' is based on the present participle form of λειτουργέω.
The translation of Ἀφορίσατε as 'set apart' is based on the imperative form of ἀφορίζω.

title: The One Spirit and the Diversity of Spiritual Gifts
english: He granted the holy apostles authority over unclean spirits, so that they could cast them out.
Indeed, he told them: 'Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those with leprosy, cast out demons. You received freely—so give freely.'
Moreover, he certainly said, 'Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons; freely you received, freely give.'
Moreover, the mighty works of divine power are not scattered apart but flow from the one Spirit.
Consider how Moses cast his staff to the ground and it became a serpent, how he turned the rivers to blood, how he drew water from the rock.
The blessed prophets have accomplished nearly all that surpasses mere word and wonder—yet we affirm that these mighty operations proceed from the one Spirit.
Still, someone may prophesy, but never apart from the Spirit.
Another may discern spirits, but only within that same Spirit.
As for what kinds of spirits are involved, we have spoken of this before.

One person confidently assures others that he knows various kinds of tongues, and also claims to interpret them—yet this gift we regard as particular, bestowed by divine economy according to need and opportunity.
Some indeed spoke in tongues though they had never learned them; others understood by interpreting, although long ago such practices were unfamiliar to the ear and not customary among such people.
Thus the divine Paul has been given to those who now insist on speaking in tongues—not as a mere share of grace, but as a sign-gift ordered for the faithful.
He also set forth this prophetic word: 'I will speak to this people in foreign tongues and with other lips, yet even so they will not believe.' (Isaiah 66:18)
And the Spirit works differently in each person as he distributes the gifts.

For just as this substantial body, formed from the earth, is composed of many parts, so too Christ’s body—that is, the Church—is constituted through the vast multitude of the holy into the most complete unity of intelligent understanding.
In this, the blessed David also says he has surrounded her with a golden garment, variegated, which I take to signify the manifold and precious charismata.
Thus, those who were to be initiators under the sun were about to speak in tongue 290 and to every nation the evident and saving proclamation of the gospel; for this purpose, he gave them tongues.
They were men of Galilee, trained according to Judea, Hebrews and from Hebrews, Medes and Parthians, and moreover Elamites—sixteen.
